records.geographic_disambiguation: Four original USGSTopo views establish distinguishable Pole/Mahogany Creek, Virgin Creek, Thousand Creek, Continental Lake, Pueblo Slough, Tumtum Lake, Trout Creek and Alvord Lake settings, ending within Alvord Desert playa. They do not establish the selected northwestern transfer out of the Mahogany Creek/Summit Lake drainage into the Sand/Virgin Creek corridor, or a selected northward through-passage from Tumtum Lake into the Trout Creek trunk. A primary-study abstract distinguishes ancient pluvial overflow north of Summit Lake from closed-basin conditions under drier climates. These are material connection questions, not a completed whole-route naming-scope hold.

A primary-study abstract distinguishes ancient pluvial overflow north of Summit Lake from closed-basin conditions under drier climates. component_scope_limits: The object spans several separately named creeks, a slough, lakes and a playa. None of those component names is assigned to the whole selected object.
The initial Pole Creek and Mahogany Creek setting is distinct from the downstream Virgin Creek corridor. An ancient northward drainage valley is not evidence of a present selected through-waterway.
Continental Lake, Tumtum Lake, Alvord Lake and Alvord Desert retain distinct waterbody or terminal-setting identities; lake/playa interiors are not renamed after adjacent creeks.

Sand Creek, Hell Creek, Sagebrush Creek, Rincon Creek, Denio Creek and the other lateral waters remain separate components or junction context. The selected line does not follow each tributary to its source.
The selected terminal is inside the mapped Alvord Desert playa, beyond the Alvord Lake setting. It is not an Alvord Lake mouth point or a marine outlet.
The maps depict intermittent channels and wetland/ditch networks. They do not establish current discharge, seasonal connectivity, operating rules or flow direction through every selected transfer.

records.candidate_name_role: representative receiving/downstream river and connected-system identity only
records.geographic_disambiguation: The selected route begins on the upper Pardo corridor east of Ibatiba, continues through Ibatiba and Iúna, reaches the Muniz Freire hydropower and Pardo–Braço Norte Esquerdo junction setting, follows that arm through Itaici and the São Simão reservoir corridor, and stays on the eastern natural river through the Santa Fé diversion setting to the western Braço Norte Direito confluence. It then follows Itapemirim through Rive, Pacotuba, the Castelo junction, Cachoeiro de Itapemirim and the lower plain to the Atlantic at Barra do Itapemirim/northern Marataízes. Five overlapping primary municipal maps, a reused state-map original, AGERH original hydrography and Quinto’s reservoir map establish the complete ordinary corridor. Independent public EIA prose distinguishes the diversion from the natural river. The downstream name is representative only.

Five overlapping primary municipal maps, a reused state-map original, AGERH original hydrography and Quinto’s reservoir map establish the complete ordinary corridor. records.supported_name_scope: representative receiving/downstream river and connected-system identity only

component_scope_limits: No uniform scalar hydronym is assigned to the complete selection. Pardo, Braço Norte Esquerdo and Itapemirim are locally distinct reaches; the unselected western Braço Norte Direito is not substituted as the headward choice.
The exact initial spring and any separate name for the short opening are unassigned. The mapped upper-valley continuation is established; no natural-source-point claim is made.

The Muniz Freire hydropower passage, São Simão reservoir passage and Santa Fé diversion/natural-channel corridor are accounted for at ordinary geographic scale. Turbine tunnels, individual structure footprints, contemporary operating levels and every small river island are not mapped onto model vertices.

Quinto’s broad Itapemirim wording at São Simão does not establish a universal local synonym for Braço Norte Esquerdo. Municipal Rio Norte/Braço Esquerdo variants are interpreted geographically with AGERH’s basin cartography, not asserted as formally registered aliases.
The selected natural eastern-arm passage is distinct from the separate western Francisco Gross reservoir and from project diversion tunnels. The officials-only PSB supplies no substantive evidence.
Ilha da Luz is identified as a hydropower setting on the mapped urban river from AGERH’s historical inventory; no separately named lake is invented.

Coastal lagoons, neighboring basins and side tributaries are excluded. Terminal correspondence is the generalized estuarine outlet beside Barra do Itapemirim/Marataízes, without exact present bank or mouth agreement.
Sources have different dates and mapping purposes. This is a bounded geographic representative-system result, not a current operational/safety review or formal naming-registry determination.

records.region: Sierra de Perijá and western Lake Maracaibo region, Colombia/Venezuela.
records.candidate_name_role: Limited receiving-system candidate for the mapped Aricuaisá–Lora junction and downstream lakeward Santa Ana; not completed representative identity of the whole selected feature and not a name for its unresolved western opening.
records.material_pending_reason: The complete selected western mountain opening and its east-northeast connector into the mapped Aricuaisá corridor remain unestablished from acquired original cartography. The general regional map, foothill cave map, historical junction diagram, nearby labels and basin descriptions do not close that material geographic link.
material_pending_components: Western selected opening and upper east-northeast connector, approximately components0–9.
records.geographic_disambiguation: Primary original-publication maps support the selected middle Aricuaisá approach, its confluence with the separate Lora, the downstream Santa Ana lowland corridor and its receiving Lago de Maracaibo setting. The acquired originals do not establish the full western mountain opening and its upper connector. Río Santa Ana is retained only as a scoped receiving-system candidate; this is one source-material-pending record, not a completed naming-scope hold or an additional access-pending case.
records.completion_scope: Primary original-publication maps support the selected middle Aricuaisá approach, its confluence with the separate Lora, the downstream Santa Ana lowland corridor and its receiving Lago de Maracaibo setting. The acquired originals do not establish the full western mountain opening and its upper connector. Río Santa Ana is retained only as a scoped receiving-system candidate; this is one source-material-pending record, not a completed naming-scope hold or an additional access-pending case.

component_scope_limits: Aricuaisá and Lora are distinct approaches. The selected middle course corresponds to Aricuaisá, while Lora approaches separately before the common Santa Ana receiver. Lora–Santa Ana prose is not applied as a uniform name to the selected Aricuaisá approach.
The western opening has no supported local name in this finding. Discovered Baracay labels remain unconfirmed, not aliases or accepted candidates.
Santa Rosa, Negro, Tucuco and Río del Norte are separate tributary or neighboring drainage names. Juan Manuel wetlands and Lago de Maracaibo are waterbody/settings, not Santa Ana aliases.
Caño Negro and Río Concepción occur in supporting lower-system prose; neither is assigned to the selected last component without map confirmation of that local label.
The actual terminal setting is Lago de Maracaibo. The retained sea classification is not treated as a direct open-Caribbean or Gulf outlet.
No uniform scalar name, Korean name, formal registry decision, precise hydronym-transition vertex, exact bank/mouth point, present-day flow condition or official total length is established.

records.region: Eastern Minas Gerais and Bahia, Brazil; selected Atlantic coastal drainage.

bounded_name_observations.name: Rio Buranhém ou Peixe
bounded_name_observations.role: Printed alternative hydronym wording on inspected trunk portions.
bounded_name_observations.scope: Does not assign either name to every small opening, feeder or lateral tributary; no universal alias boundary is established.

records.geographic_disambiguation: Original IBGE municipal maps support Rio Buranhém as the representative identity of the selected connected river system. The inspected trunk is labelled Rio Buranhém ou Peixe, with geographic correspondence from the western headward setting through Guaratinga and south of Eunápolis to the Atlantic estuary at Porto Seguro. This does not name every initial feeder or tributary. Accepted, scalar and Korean names remain unset.

naming_scope_details.component_scope_limits: Representative identity is supported by overlapping original cartography from the western opening to the actual sea terminal. It is not a uniform scalar name for every selected reach or an assertion that all feeders share the trunk name.

reconstruction_rule: Start from the pinned r46 cumulative index and apply later append-only deltas in verified commit order, rejecting duplicate IDs. Keep base records, scope clauses, region qualifiers and assessment histories unchanged. Apply explicit status-list changes. Subtract all recorded IDs from the exact eligible initial inventory to recover unrecorded targets; pending IDs remain recorded but are not completed source reviews.
publication_boundary: Own factual name/scope findings, public official URLs, bounded geometry metadata and public continuity pins only. No original maps, crops, complete coordinates or private source/derivative/registration fingerprints. Official hosting does not establish source redistribution rights.

research_order.progress_rule: Follow the actual continental order: Americas, Asia, Africa, Europe, then other, with all rivers before lakes. Preserve original queue IDs and ranks for continuity; apply documented geographic deferrals without counting them as name research, and place deferred objects into their corrected later phase by length-descending, stable-ID order. Prior candidate and scope-held assessments remain unresolved where stated.
